messages:
Alex C: FYI — customer AcmeCorp reporting sudden 429s on their dedicated capacity since ~03:10 UTC. They say traffic should hit their reserved pool but we're seeing requests routed to shared pools and getting throttled. Filing here before pager.
SRE-Bot: alert: DedicatedPoolThrottled cluster=us-west-2 pool=shared-001 spike=75% since 03:08 UTC :warning:
Priya S: @Alex C can you paste the original request headers and a short repro? also tenant id + pool id from the ticket
Alex C: tenant=acme-42, expected_pool=dedicated-acme-42, observed_pool=shared-001
Alex C: repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>"
  -H "X-Redwood-Tier: Gold"
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-42"
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Alex C: When I replayed from our proxy logs the routing decision logged selected_pool=shared-001 even though routing table has rule matching tier=gold -> dedicated-acme-42
Maya R: I pulled the raw control-plane routing event for those requests. Here's the relevant snippet from the route matcher logs (sanitized):
```
[03:09:02] route_eval id=abc123 tenant=acme-42 labels={tier: "Gold\n", region: "us-west-2"} -> match_rules: [tier=="gold"] -> selected_pool=shared-001
```
Maya R: Note the label value contains a trailing newline and capital G. Our rule expects lowercase exact match "gold" (case-sensitive) -> so it falls through to default routing which picks shared pool
Priya S: ohhh. so parser didn't normalize labels (trim/casefold). That would explain thousands of requests being misrouted.
EngInfra: Confirmed. The label parser in control-plane v2.7.1 does exact string compare. We introduced stricter validation last release and inadvertently rejected normalization for headers. There's a unit test gap.
Alex C: Customer is seeing ~20% elevated p50 latency and frequent 429s. They asked for ETA on fix and temporary mitigation.
Maya R: Temporary mitigation options:
- Add a backward-compatible matcher for tier variants (Gold|gold|"Gold\n") via regex in routing table (fast, low-risk)
- Add request-header sanitization at proxy layer to trim/lowcase X-Redwood-Tier (requires a quick config push to edge)
- Manual route override to pin tenant->pool (requires DB write + restart of routing cache)
Priya S: I prefer edge sanitization + quick regex rule. Manual DB override is risky during peak. EngInfra, how fast can we ship edge header normalization as a config change?
EngInfra: Edge config rollout: we can push header normalization rule to the gateway within ~30 minutes and it can be canaried to 10% then 100%. No code change. Regex rule on control-plane routing table deploy would be ~45-60m with migration check.
SRE-Bot: incident-level suggestion: P2 (customer impact, partial degradation). Log ingest shows ~11k misrouted requests since 03:05 UTC.
Alex C: I'll ask Acme to switch to lower QPS for the next 1hr and share we have a mitigation plan. Also requesting access to their recent request dump for more samples.
Maya R: Root cause summary: label parsing is case-sensitive and does not trim whitespace/newline. Small data/agent clients sometimes send "Gold\n" (from CLI wrappers). Control plane rule uses exact match -> fallthrough -> shared pool -> throttling.
Priya S: Postmortem action items:
- (EngInfra) Hotfix: push gateway header normalization and add control-plane regex fallback in routing table — target <2h
- (EngInfra) Patch control-plane label parser to normalize (trim + toLower) and add unit tests — target next patch release
- (SRE) Add alert: unusual pool selection delta for tenants with reserved pools (delta > 5%)
- (Support) Customer comms + temporary credit offer if SLA breach
EngInfra: I'll start the gateway config change now and open a canary. Will report back at +15m.
Alex C: thx. keeping Acme updated. tagging participants here so we can correlate logs: @Maya R @Priya S @EngInfra
Priya S: :eyes: keep me posted. once gateway fix is live i'll coordinate with support for rollback plan if needed.
Maya R: after gateway change we should reprocess a sample of logs and confirm route_eval now logs tier:"gold" and selected_pool=dedicated-acme-42
SRE-Bot: update: canary push started to edges (10% traffic) at 03:24 UTC
EngInfra: canary looks good after 5m. no errors. promoting to 50% now.
EngInfra: promoted to 100% at 03:30 UTC. routing logs now show normalized labels and selection to dedicated-acme-42 for tenant acme-42. Throttles dropped to baseline.
Alex C: Customer confirms reduced 429s and latency recovering. They'll leave the reduced QPS window but want permanent fix timeline.
EngInfra: Opening a PR for parser normalization + tests. Will target the next patch (v2.7.2) and schedule a canary tomorrow. I'll include a migration note about older agents that might send malformed headers.
Priya S: great. I'll draft customer note and SLA remediation language. Marking incident resolved (P2 -> monitoring) once post-deploy tests pass tomorrow.
Alex C: thanks team. leaving this thread open for final postmortem links and the PR number. :thumbsup:
